perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He knows Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist at his construction company; they are friendly, professional colleagues who usually interact when he comes into the office for paperwork or project updates.
- Over the past few days, he noticed Elizabeth was unusually curt/short with him.
- He wondered whether he had upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- He asked her if he had done something to upset her because she seemed off with him.
- Elizabeth told him no, not at all; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic after learning it was not anger toward him but personal stress.
- He offered to be someone she could talk to and suggested a coffee break.
- Elizabeth accepted the coffee break and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; to Keith, they seemed quite severe.
- He thanked her for sharing and suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help.
- Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, he noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn.
- He thought his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped, and that he was there to support her no matter what.
- Elizabeth said he didn’t overstep, appreciated his concern, and said it was just a lot to think about.
- Following that conversation, Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative of his concern.
- He believes she values his support and feels more comfortable around him now.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always there if she needs to chat or take a break together.
- Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- He intends to maintain this supportive relationship with her.
